title: The clock guard before the first floor and the book's walk to the day -- shared cases for iOS, Windows and Android

sources.decision: decision 188 of the author of Montana, 2026-10-25 18:45 UTC

conventions: d = the device's UTC day; heard = the days named by node Date headers received in this run (any door; c = max(M, heard))
M, H, Hc = device state sealed beside the pipe book, surviving a restart; never in the archive
F = the floor day = d - floorLag, applied to every pipe of the book
a step is one read of the book; 'restart: true' starts a new process run before the read (memory and the per-run trace memory are new, the sealed M/H/Hc stay)
trace: the lines written by that step, in order; [] means none. floor_held is written once per run and again only when d, c or left change
H and Hc are cleared whenever the floor applies (rule 2 or rule 3); after the first floor the guard is never asked again (rule 4)
start 'after_case_2' = the sealed state M 20760, H 20800, Hc 20760, the book not floored, a new run

a book with no pipe does not ask the rule: M is still raised by what is heard, H and Hc are not started; the rule is asked when the first pipe arrives, and a new pipe never resets H (chairman 19:23 UTC, point 3)

rule 4 is kept in the sealed guard state: once the first floor applies, the guard records it beside M/H/Hc (cleared H, Hc), even when the book's own write fails, so a restart that reads the book whole floors on d without asking the guard (case 15 = the chairman's case 9b, 21:05 UTC)

a restore asks the guard: while the guard withholds the first floor, restored keys are floored by the guard's day (eraseDay - 1: nothing floors) and wait with the book; otherwise a restore floors by max(d, M); the restore writes no trace of its own (case 16)
M is raised by any node answer that carries a Date header, whatever its status (a refusal is an answer); a cancelled request or a transport failure does not raise it
with no confirmed source the trace writes c=none (one format on every port)
floor_held is written again only when d, c or left changes; early and floor results write nothing and reset nothing, so held -> early -> held at the same values writes one line

an unreadable guard record is never overwritten and the guard does not withhold: the floor applies on d as by rule 2, traced floor_free d=D c=none (case 18); a failed write of the guard record is retried at the next decision

case 13 ordering: a parallel reader may get the walked copy before its write lands; no read after the floor day hands out a whole key, and no step moves a floor day back; a refused book write is retried at the first read at least 60 s after the refusal

cases.note: the restore asks the guard (chairman 22:04 UTC, main point)

expect.restore: the restored key stays whole, as the book

cases.note: point 2: a read before any answer decides on the sealed M, the next read after an answer decides again; the chairman's example used d 20761, where rule 2 already floors (d <= c + 1), so d 20763 is used here
point 3: an unreadable guard record is not overwritten and the guard does not withhold

case_13_also: the walk of the book in memory happens on the FIRST READ of a new day, before the book is handed to the caller, in the running process (no restart needed); it asks the guard first, so it may still be held

the walked book is written to disk at once, atomically (write the new sealed form beside the old one, then replace it), and only then handed out; if the write fails, the floored copy stays in memory and is handed out floored, and the next read writes again; nothing whole is ever written back
idempotent: a second read on the same day changes nothing and writes nothing; no step ever moves a floor day back
a pipe born during a hold stays whole until the floor applies, then the floor takes it like every other pipe
